answers.question: Retrieve the first name, last name and address of all employees who work for the 'Research' department.
answers.sql:
SELECT b.Fname, b.Lname, b.Address
FROM Employee b
JOIN Department a ON b.Dno = a.Dnumber
WHERE a.Dname = 'Research';

answers.question: For every project located in 'Stafford', list the project number, the controlling department number, and the department manager's last name, address and birth date.
answers.sql:
SELECT c.Pnumber, d.Dnumber, e.Lname, e.Address, e.Bdate
FROM Project c
JOIN Department d ON c.Dnum = d.Dnumber
JOIN Employee e ON d.Mgr_ssn = e.Ssn
WHERE d.Dlocation = 'Stafford';

answers.question: Find the sum of the salaries, the maximum salary, the minimum salary and the average salary of employees of the 'Research' department.
answers.sql:
SELECT SUM(b.Salary), MAX(b.Salary), MIN(b.Salary), AVG(b.Salary)
FROM Employee b
JOIN Department a ON b.Dno = a.Dnumber
WHERE a.Dname = 'Research';

answers.question: For each project, retrieve the project number, the project name and the number of employees who work on that project.
answers.sql:
SELECT P.Pnumber, P.Pname, COUNT(Works_On.Essn) AS Num
FROM Project P
JOIN Works_On ON P.Pnumber = Works_On.Pno
GROUP BY P.Pnumber, P.Pname;

answers.question: For each project on which more than two employees work, retrieve the project name and the number of employees.
answers.sql:
SELECT c.Pname, COUNT(DISTINCT b.Essn) AS Num
FROM Project c
JOIN Works_On b ON c.Pnumber = b.Pno
GROUP BY c.Pnumber, c.Pname
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT b.Essn) > 2;

answers.question: Show the department name and the total hours worked on projects controlled by that department.
answers.sql:
SELECT d.Dname, SUM(l.Hours) AS Total_Hours
FROM Department d
JOIN Employee b ON b.Dno = d.Dnumber
JOIN Works_On l ON b.Ssn = l.Essn
GROUP BY d.Dname;

answers.question: Create a view named Dept_Summary that shows each department name, number of employees and average salary.
answers.sql:
CREATE VIEW Dept_Summary AS
SELECT a.Dname, COUNT(b.Ssn) AS Num_Employees, AVG(b.Salary) AS Avg_Salary
FROM Department a
LEFT JOIN Employee b ON a.Dnumber = b.Dno
GROUP BY a.Dname;

answers.question: Retrieve the SSNs of employees who work on project number 1 but not on project number 2, using EXCEPT.
Show last name, salary and a column Band that is 'Low' when salary is below 30000, 'Mid' when it is from 30000 to 40000 and 'High' otherwise.
answers.sql:
SELECT Lname, Salary,
       CASE WHEN Salary < 30000 THEN 'Low'
            WHEN Salary BETWEEN 30000 AND 40000 THEN 'Mid'
            ELSE 'High' END AS Band
FROM Employee;
